title: On the road in 1930 with shows, doing everything, show-business discipline
summary: In 1930 he plays drums, piano, sax, sings and dances with shows; he recalls show people's strict discipline and the Billboard blacklist.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: What were you playing at that time? Were you playing drums then?

Yes. But I wasn't quite sure whether I played drums or piano because sometimes you'd catch me, I would be playing saxophone. Sometimes I'd be singing. Some places I'd be dancing. Some places I'd get on the show, I'd be doing everything because I remember in 1930 I joined a show and there were 3 pianists. A piano player by the name of Troy and Floyd; Washington, was his last name. That's all I knew because they only called him Washington because in those days they only called, Washington. Meanwhile I had had the fortune of meeting the guys that made the QRS Little records, the fellows like Lou Louis. I have been fortunate enough to have met Seminole because I was moving all the time and what was so fortunate -
Were you on your own now or were you still -
I was on my own, because in those days, Milt, you know good and well that when you joined a show

had to be you were recommended from your minister or your rabbi or somebody and you had to be 25 years old before you drank alcohol. You just didn't come out and say, I'm 18, I'm eligible to drink. You didn't go into no nightclub. But at the same time, that way we were juveniles and you started in show business young. You had a whole lot of fathers and uncles and mothers out here, you see, and what was so remarkable about it, they taught us moral and civic discipline. Because you remember at that time the Billboard had a thing called the blacklist. If you picked up that issue and saw your name on the blacklist, that meant that you was grounded for a year. It was impossible for you to get on a (Sells-Floto) it was impossible for you to get on a Ethel Waters or a Ma Rainey or a Whitman Sisters show. It was impossible for you to get a job shining shoes on the Sahara Desert.
